name: NavigationTitle
purpose: Stack chrome for the current view controller (UINavigationBar / Android Toolbar). Title, back, and bar items. Formerly NavigationBar — renamed to avoid confusion with Navigation (tab controller). Not a site link row — that is Navbar. Root tabs are Navigation. Not TitleBar (sidebar brand).
scenarios: Show the current screen title at the top of AppShell
Pop the active tab's stack with a back control labeled by the previous title
Keep trailing bar-button items on the same bar as the title across three ends

backLabel.description: Previous controller title on the back control. Default Back.

onBack.description: Pops the active tab stack. Omit on the root controller so no back control is shown.

leading.description: Leading slot when there is no back control.

states.name: nested
states.description: Stack depth > 1; back control pops to the previous title.

antiPatterns: Do not put root destinations in NavigationTitle; those belong on Navigation (the tab controller).
Do not use Navbar (site links) as AppShell stack chrome.
Do not confuse NavigationTitle with TitleBar — TitleBar is sidebar brand in Navigation header.
Do not push onto the stack when switching tabs; switch the tab's own stack.

keyboard: Tab moves through back and trailing controls
a11y.focus: Back is a real button; the title is a heading.
a11y.labeling: The title is an h1 of the current screen; back uses the previous title as its label.

responsive.strategy: One bar. Compact centers the title. At 48rem the title leads. Safe-area top inset on the bar. No viewport size @media.

breakpoints.compact: Centered title, back on the leading edge, 44px hit area, safe-area top inset.
breakpoints.medium: Leading title beside back, same controls.

rtl.strategy: Logical CSS; the back chevron mirrors under [dir=rtl].

mechanics: NavigationTitle (formerly NavigationBar) is stack chrome (UINavigationBar / Toolbar) for the current view controller, not a site link row and not the tab controller (Navigation) and not sidebar brand (TitleBar). Mount in AppShell header / Vue #header. Title is an h1. When onBack is set, the leading edge is a back button labeled with the previous controller title; otherwise leading renders (React prop / Vue #leading). trailing is bar-button items (React prop / Vue #trailing). backLabel defaults to Back. Chrome row: .cu-navigation-title__frame uses min-block-size calc(var(--cu-control-size-active) + 2 * var(--cu-space-1)) — same formula as Navigation __header and NavAccountCard. Root also carries legacy .cu-navigation-bar class during transition. Compact centers the title; from 48rem the title leads. Pair with useTabStacks: selectTab does not push; onBack should call pop. NavigationBar remains a deprecated export alias of NavigationTitle.
usage: Import NavigationTitle and useTabStacks from the React or Vue umbrella (NavigationBar still works as a deprecated alias).
Render title from stacks.current.title. Pass backLabel={stacks.previous?.title} and onBack={stacks.canPop ? stacks.pop : undefined}.
Place NavigationTitle in AppShell header / #header. Root destinations belong on Navigation; sidebar brand is TitleBar in Navigation header — not this component.
Call stacks.push when opening a nested screen. Call stacks.selectTab when the user picks a Navigation item — that must not push.
Do not hardcode rem bar heights; densify via --cu-control-size-active with density.css.

exports.name: NavigationTitle
exports.description: Stack chrome: title, back, leading, and trailing bar items.

exports.description: Per-tab stacks. selectTab does not push. pop is back.
